newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura Securities chairman says to quit JSDA post.
newsitem.headline: Nomura Securities chairman says to quit JSDA post.

text.p: The chairman of Nomura Securities Co Ltd Masashi Suzuki said on Monday that he would resign as head of the Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA).
Suzuki told a news conference he wanted Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd chairman Tsugio Yukihira to take over as JSDA chairman.
Yukihira is currently JSDA vice chairman.
He said his resignation would take effect when the next JSDA chairman is selected.
Nomura said last week that two of its directors were involved in suspected illegal deals in which substantial sums of Nomura's money were moved into a corporate customer's account.
Suzuki told reporters that he had decided to resign as JSDA chairman to take responsibility for the scandal.

Earlier on Monday, Shoichiro Toyoda, the chairman of Japan's powerful business lobby, the Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren), said the chairman and president of Nomura Securities had both resigned their senior Keidanren positions as of Monday.
